summary.text: 睡 combines 目, which contributes an eye-related association, with 垂 as a sound element. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; current meanings include “sleep” and “doze.”

formation.text: This is a phonosemantic compound: 目 contributes an eye-related meaning, and 垂 supplies the sound. The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting.”

components.text: 目 means “eye” and contributes an eye-related semantic association in 睡; it does not depict a whole sleeping scene.
垂 is identified as the sound element. Baxter–Sagart reconstructions show a close match before 睡’s additional *-s ending, supporting but not proving this role.

sound.text: In this reconstruction system, 睡 has the same reconstructed segments as 垂 before an added *-s ending.
The locally recorded modern Mandarin readings differ; this present-day comparison does not itself establish their historical sound relationship.

history.text: The traditional written analysis has 睡 formed from 目 and 垂. A later commentary connects 目 with drooping eyelids; that explanation interprets the graph but does not demonstrate its earliest construction.

The Qin manuscript database records a form labeled 睡.法4, though its glyph image was unavailable for comparison. The available seal-script depiction is a modern redrawing, not an ancient artifact; the evidence here therefore does not document a sequence of graphic changes.

uncertainties.text: The earliest physical attestation and detailed graphic evolution of 睡 remain unresolved. Transmitted text examples do not establish the dates of surviving manuscripts or a chronology from sleeping while seated to broader sleep and lying down.

The reconstructed sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis but does not prove it by itself. The Mandarin readings are recorded in local data; direct Unihan character pages could not be verified.

senses.period: dating unresolved; gloss in the transmitted Shuowen account
senses.text: The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting.” It provides an early lexical framing but does not establish manuscript dates or that this was the word’s original meaning.

senses.period: attested in transmitted classical examples; dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted text examples use 睡 for sleeping or dozing. The evidence does not establish when this broader use arose relative to the sitting-sleep gloss.

senses.period: Qing example recorded; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: A later example is glossed “lie down.” The evidence does not establish a semantic path from sleeping to lying down.

limitations.text: The evidence records distinct historical and current uses but does not establish a chronological chain among sleeping while seated, broader sleep, and lying down; no semantic-development links are asserted.

overview.text: 睡 combines 目, “eye,” with 垂 as a sound element. Its traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting”; today it means “sleep” or “doze.”

components.text: 目 links 睡 to the eyes, a body part associated with sleep.
In the cited reconstruction, 睡 matches 垂 but has an added ending.

relationships.text: Within 睡, 目 contributes the eye-related semantic association in the traditional analysis.

The traditional analysis assigns 垂 a sound role. Baxter–Sagart reconstructs 垂 as *[d]o[j] and 睡 as *[d]o[j]-s, a close same-system comparison with an added ending in 睡; this supports but does not independently prove the role.
The traditional gloss is “sleep while sitting.” It provides an early lexical framing but does not establish manuscript dates or that this was the word’s original meaning.
Transmitted text examples use 睡 for sleeping or dozing. The evidence does not establish when this broader use arose relative to the sitting-sleep gloss.
A later example is glossed “lie down.” The evidence does not establish a semantic path from sleeping to lying down.

limitations.text: The available candidate is a modern redrawing of 睡 in Shuowen seal-script style, rather than an image of a dated historical artifact. It cannot show when this form was used or trace the character’s graphic development; the earliest physical form remains unresolved.
